sections.heading: What builders need
sections.content: Quality comes first: poor training data is extremely challenging for a model to overcome. Builders also need volume—potentially thousands of high-quality examples in advanced fields such as chemistry, mathematics, and physics—and speed: providers should be able to turn data around in days. Lord says expert access helps meet the quality and volume needs, citing outreach to top students at Stanford, Berkeley, and MIT for physics data.

sections.heading: Why those needs matter
sections.content: Lord says much of the recent improvement has shifted to post-training, as labs had largely absorbed the knowledge available on the internet. Research teams test hypotheses with small data collections; when one shows gains, they expand that pipeline and may drop other projects. Fast delivery lets them scale the data that is working. Providers also need to assess whether individual data units improve a capability, and work with researchers to share what they are seeing and how the data might best be used for training.
